assessment.nobel_worthiness: A consequential, empirically grounded account of how technology, trade exposure, and task change reshape employment and wage inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn, and Hanson form a coherent core for the task, technology, and trade-shock evidence.
assessment.maturity: The research agenda has accumulated extensive evidence and substantially influenced labour-market analysis and policy debate.
uncertainties: Separating the distinct contributions of automation, trade, and broader regional change remains difficult.
The appropriate laureate set is contestable given related contributions by other labour economists.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative-data research transformed measurement of intergenerational mobility and revealed strong geographic variation with major policy relevance.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren, and Friedman are central to the linked mobility measurement and place-based evidence.
assessment.maturity: The work is mature, widely used, and has generated an enduring empirical research program.
uncertainties: Descriptive mobility measures do not by themselves establish the causal mechanisms behind geographic differences.
Credit allocation is challenging because the program is collaborative and overlaps with adjacent work on inequality and public economics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Audit and correspondence designs supplied especially vivid and influential evidence on labour-market discrimination.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan are clear leading contributors to the canonical modern correspondence-study evidence.
assessment.maturity: The approach has been replicated, extended across settings, and remains central to empirical discrimination research.
uncertainties: Audit-study estimates can be sensitive to how signals and employer responses map into broader discrimination mechanisms.
A prize centered on this evidence would require careful treatment of important earlier and parallel contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This body of work made early-life health and skill formation central economic determinants of later-life outcomes.
assessment.attribution: Currie, Almond, and Cunha represent complementary empirical and conceptual contributions to the stated discovery.
assessment.maturity: Multiple decades of evidence across health, education, and labour outcomes support a mature research program.
uncertainties: The discovery combines several related mechanisms rather than one sharply bounded breakthrough.
Long-run causal estimates and policy transportability remain heterogeneous across contexts.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The rehabilitation of monopsony as a practically important feature of labour markets changed analysis of wages, employer power, and labour-market policy.
assessment.attribution: Manning provided the foundational modern framework, while Naidu is a prominent contributor to its empirical development.
assessment.maturity: Theory and a broadening empirical literature now provide substantial support for the importance of imperfect competition.
uncertainties: The magnitude and policy implications of monopsony vary markedly across labour markets.
The candidate grouping spans foundational theory and later empirical work, complicating attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theoretical and empirical work on adverse selection gave insurance economics a powerful framework for measuring information problems and welfare consequences.
assessment.attribution: Finkelstein, Einav, and Salanie are appropriate representatives of the integration of theory, data, and institutional evidence.
assessment.maturity: The research has been deeply absorbed into health, insurance, and public-economics research.
uncertainties: The extent of adverse selection and offsetting advantageous selection differs across markets.
Attribution must distinguish this contribution from the broader economics of insurance and health care.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structural modelling of labour supply, taxes, and household intertemporal choices greatly improved the analysis of behavioural responses to policy.
assessment.attribution: Blundell, Meghir, and MaCurdy are major and identifiable contributors to the structural labour-supply tradition.
assessment.maturity: The approach has had sustained influence in public finance, labour economics, and policy simulation.
uncertainties: Structural conclusions depend on modelling choices and on the stability of estimated preferences and constraints.
The work is a broad methodological tradition with many important contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on teacher quality, school accountability, and educational production placed learning outcomes and credible evaluation at the center of education policy economics.
assessment.attribution: Kane, Hanushek, and Woessmann each made major contributions to the evidence and policy framework represented here.
assessment.maturity: The agenda has generated a large evidence base and durable influence on education-policy design.
uncertainties: Effects of accountability and teacher policies can depend heavily on institutional context and implementation.
The candidate package is broad, and the balance between its component discoveries is not fully settled.
